question: If I work while I'm incarcerated, in a prison job or on work release, how is my pay set, what can the state deduct from my earnings and in what order, and what do I get back when I'm released?

negative: child working under the industries program

gold_sections.why: Every capable inmate must work; the Board may (not must) create an incentive pay scale; any such pay goes to the trust fund and up to 80 percent can be deducted for restitution and dependent care; excludes TCI and private-industry pay.
The Texas Minimum Wage Act exempts employers of people working while imprisoned in TDCJ's institutional division or confined in a local jail.

Private sector prison industries (PIE) jobs must pay at least the PIECP wage: the employer's own wage for similar work in the local workforce development area, or Texas Workforce Commission occupational wage data if it has no comparable workers; the Board may allow a federal-minimum-wage start period.
The Board sets by rule the amount and disbursement of deductions from PIE wages, consistent with the federal PIECP statute.

Inmate money is held in a TDCJ account; court-ordered withdrawals (including child support orders from anyone) follow a six-step schedule of priorities; holds and withdrawals for debts owed the department; court orders come before the department's 501.063 balance; escape forfeits the account.

On discharge or release: civilian clothing, the trust account money, release cash and an ID certificate if available; $100 ($50 + $50) and transportation for those who must report to a parole officer, $100 and transportation home or to a transit point for those who need not; no cash on transfer to a state jail or a felony detainer.
Texas Correctional Industries: the Board may (not must) adopt an incentive pay scale; pay earned is apportioned the same way as PIE wages under 497.0581 rules.

TCI contracts with private businesses must meet all PIECP requirements; service contracts may skip the prevailing-wage requirement only if they pay at least the federal minimum wage, and 497.058 does not apply to them.
Defines Texas Correctional Industries and 'work program participant'.
Board certifies PIE programs in TDCJ and county facilities under 18 U.S.C. 1761; defines 'participant'.

gold_sections.ref: Tex. Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 14.006
gold_sections.why: Court fees in an inmate's lawsuit are withdrawn from the trust account (20 percent of six months' deposits, then 10 percent monthly) until paid or release.

gold_sections.ref: Tex. Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 63.007
gold_sections.why: A writ of garnishment may be issued against money in the inmate trust fund.
TDCJ may seize an inmate's trust fund for intentional damage to state property only after a hearing, with damages capped at the property's value.

County jail time served intermittently during off-work hours or weekends: the court may have the employer deduct pay and use it for dependents, expenses, jail maintenance and restitution, fines and costs; the condition does not bind the employer except child support withholding.
County jail work release program: the trial judge may order a low-risk defendant into it.
Restitution center (community corrections facility) salary goes to the director, who deducts food/housing/supervision, travel, dependent support and restitution and holds the rest for release.
A court may require a misdemeanant to reimburse the county $25 a day for jail confinement, billed by the sheriff at discharge.

A defendant unable to pay a fine and costs may work them off in the county jail industries program, workhouse, county farm or public projects; confinement and labor are each rated at $150 a day, and the court or sheriff may add two days' credit per day in an approved work program.
County jail labor (jail industries or manual labor) earns one day of sentence credit per day worked rather than wages.
County jail industries revenue goes to the county general fund as reimbursement for the cost of confinement.
A pre-parolee moved from a community residential facility to parole receives any balance of the 501.015 release money.
On release TDCJ gives the person a copy of the permanent work record.

nuggets.text: Texas's minimum wage law does not apply to work done by a person while imprisoned in the TDCJ institutional division or confined in a local jail.
nuggets.quote: An employer is exempt from this chapter with respect to the employment of a person who performs services while imprisoned in the institutional division of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice or while confined in a local jail.

nuggets.text: For regular prison work programs, the Texas Board of Criminal Justice may (but is not required to) adopt an incentive pay scale, with pay levels meant to teach diligent work rather than to reward inmates.
nuggets.quote: The board may develop by rule and the department may administer an incentive pay scale program for inmates required to work in agricultural, industrial, or other work programs. In developing the program, the board shall set pay levels not to unjustly reward inmates, but rather to instruct inmates on the virtues of diligent participation in the workplace.

nuggets.text: Any incentive pay is deposited in the inmate's trust fund, and TDCJ may deduct up to 80 percent of it for restitution and dependent care the inmate owes.
nuggets.quote: The department shall deposit an amount earned by an inmate under this subsection into the inmate's trust fund and may deduct not more than 80 percent of the amount deposited under this subsection for payment of restitution and dependent care owed by the inmate.

nuggets.text: For Texas Correctional Industries jobs the Board may (but need not) adopt an incentive pay scale, and any pay earned is apportioned the same way the Board's rules split private-industry (PIE) wages.
nuggets.quote: The board may develop by rule and the department may administer an incentive pay scale for work program participants consistent with rules adopted by the board under Subchapter C. Prison industries may be financed through contributions donated for this purpose by private businesses contracting with the department. The department shall apportion pay earned by a work program participant in the same manner as is required by rules adopted by the board under Section 497.0581.

nuggets.text: In a private sector prison industries program, Board rules must require pay of at least the PIECP wage as computed by the Texas Workforce Commission, though the Board may let employers pay the federal minimum wage for the first two months.
nuggets.quote: be paid not less than the prison industry enhancement certification program (PIECP) wage as computed by the Texas Workforce Commission, except that: (1) the board may permit employers to pay a participant the federal minimum wage for the two-month period beginning on the date participation begins;

nuggets.text: The Board decides by rule how much is deducted from private-industry wages and where those deductions go.
nuggets.quote: The board by rule shall determine the amount of deductions to be taken from wages received by the participant under this subchapter and the disbursement of those deductions.

nuggets.text: When a court notifies TDCJ, the department must withdraw from the inmate's account whatever the court has ordered the inmate to pay; for child support it must act on any valid court order, whether the court or another person provides it.
nuggets.quote: On notification by a court, the department shall withdraw from an inmate's account any amount the inmate is ordered to pay by order of the court under this subsection. On receipt of a valid court order requiring an inmate to pay child support, the department shall withdraw the appropriate amount from the inmate's account under this subsection, regardless of whether the court order is provided by the court or another person.

nuggets.text: Court-ordered withdrawals are paid in a fixed order: first child support, second restitution, third reimbursement to the Health and Human Services Commission for assistance for the inmate's child's health needs.
nuggets.quote: (1) as payment in full for all orders for child support; (2) as payment in full for all orders for restitution; (3) as payment in full for all orders for reimbursement of the Health and Human Services Commission for financial assistance provided for the child's health needs

nuggets.text: Next come court fees and costs, then fines, then any other court order, judgment or writ.
nuggets.quote: (4) as payment in full for all orders for court fees and costs; (5) as payment in full for all orders for fines; and (6) as payment in full for any other court order, judgment, or writ.

nuggets.text: TDCJ may also hold or withdraw account money to recover what the inmate owes the department for indigent supplies, medical copayments, destroyed state property or other debts.
nuggets.quote: to recover money the inmate owes the department for indigent supplies, medical copayments, destruction of state property, or other indebtedness

nuggets.text: Court-ordered withdrawals come before TDCJ applies deposits to any unpaid balance the inmate owes the department under Government Code 501.063 (a section cited here but not in the downloaded statutes).
nuggets.quote: The department shall withdraw money from an inmate's account under Subsection (e) before the department applies a deposit to that account toward any unpaid balance owed to the department by the inmate under Section 501.063.

nuggets.text: On discharge or release on parole, mandatory supervision or conditional pardon, TDCJ must give the person suitable civilian clothing, the money held in the trust account, release cash under subsection (b), and a personal identification certificate if one is available.
nuggets.quote: When an inmate is discharged or is released on parole, mandatory supervision, or conditional pardon, the department shall provide the inmate with: (1) suitable civilian clothing; (2) money held in the inmate's trust account by the director; (3) cash, in an amount and in the manner described by Subsection (b); and (4) a personal identification certificate obtained under Section 501.0165, if available.

nuggets.text: A person released on parole, mandatory supervision or conditional pardon is entitled to $100 and transportation at TDCJ's expense to the place the parole division requires them to report: $50 on leaving and $50 on first reporting to the parole officer.
nuggets.quote: the inmate is entitled to receive $100 from the department and transportation at the expense of the department to the location at which the inmate is required to report to a parole officer by the parole division. The inmate shall receive $50 on release from the institution and $50 on initially reporting to a parole officer

nuggets.text: When a judge lets a county jail sentence be served intermittently during off-work hours or on weekends, the court may require pay deductions, and the money may be used as the court directs for dependents' support, the defendant's documented expenses, reimbursing the county for jail upkeep, and installments on restitution, fines and court costs; the condition does not bind the employer, except for child support income withholding.
nuggets.quote: The money received by the court under this section may be used to pay the following expenses as directed by the court: (1) the support of the defendant's dependents, if necessary; (2) the defendant's documented personal, business, and travel expenses; (3) reimbursement of the general fund of the county for the maintenance of the defendant in jail; and (4) installment payments on restitution, fines, and court costs ordered by the court. (c) The condition imposed under Subsection (b) of this article is not binding on an employer, except that income withheld for child support is governed by Chapter 158, Family Code.

nuggets.text: In a restitution center, the director deposits the defendant's salary into a fund given to the defendant on release, after deducting the center's cost of food, housing and supervision, travel and incidental expenses, dependents' support, and restitution to victims.
nuggets.quote: The director shall deposit the salary into a fund to be given to the defendant on release after the director deducts: (1) the cost to the center for the defendant's food, housing, and supervision; (2) the necessary expense for the defendant's travel to and from work and community service projects, and other incidental expenses of the defendant; (3) support of the defendant's dependents; and (4) restitution to the victims of an offense committed by the defendant.

nuggets.text: The PIECP wage is the employer's own wage for similar work in the local workforce development area where the work is done; if the employer has no comparable non-inmate employees there, the prevailing wage comes from Texas Workforce Commission occupational wage data.
nuggets.quote: (1) the PIECP wage is the wage paid by the employer for work of a similar nature in the location in which the work is performed; (2) in the event that the employer has no employees other than those employed under this subchapter performing work of a similar nature within the location, the prevailing wage for work of a similar nature is determined by reference to openings and wages by occupation data collected by the labor market information department of the Texas Workforce Commission; and (3) the location in which work is performed is the local workforce development area in which the work is performed.

nuggets.text: A Texas Correctional Industries contract with a private business to provide services must meet the federal PIECP requirements except the prevailing-wage rule, as long as it pays at least the federal minimum wage.
nuggets.quote: be certified by the board as complying with all requirements of the Private Sector/Prison Industry Enhancement Certification Program operated by the Bureau of Justice Assistance and authorized by 18 U.S.C. Section 1761, other than a requirement relating to the payment of prevailing wages, so long as the contract requires payment of not less than the federal minimum wage

nuggets.text: An inmate who escapes or attempts to escape forfeits to TDCJ all the money in the inmate's account at that time.
nuggets.quote: An inmate who escapes or attempts to escape from the custody of the department forfeits to the department all of the money held by the department in the inmate's account at the time of the escape or attempted escape.

nuggets.text: If a court orders an inmate who filed a lawsuit to pay court fees and costs, the trust account is charged the lesser of 20 percent of the prior six months' deposits or the full amount, then each month the lesser of 10 percent of that month's deposits or the unpaid balance, until paid or release.
nuggets.section: Tex. Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 14.006
nuggets.quote: On the court's order, the inmate shall pay an amount equal to the lesser of: (1) 20 percent of the preceding six months' deposits to the inmate's trust account; or (2) the total amount of court fees and costs. (c) In each month following the month in which payment is made under Subsection (b), the inmate shall pay an amount equal to the lesser of: (1) 10 percent of that month's deposits to the trust account; or (2) the total amount of court fees and costs that remain unpaid. (d) Payments under Subsection (c) shall continue until the total amount of court fees and costs are paid or until the inmate is released from confinement.

nuggets.text: A creditor can get a writ of garnishment against money held for an inmate in the TDCJ inmate trust fund.
nuggets.section: Tex. Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 63.007
nuggets.quote: A writ of garnishment may be issued against an inmate trust fund held under the authority of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice under Section 501.014, Government Code, to encumber money that is held for the benefit of an inmate in the fund.

nuggets.text: TDCJ can collect for intentional damage to state property only after a hearing, capped at the property's value; if the inmate is found liable, it may seize the inmate's trust fund.
nuggets.quote: Damages may be awarded to the department only after a hearing and may not exceed the value of the property damaged. (c) If at a hearing it is determined that an inmate is liable for property damage, the department may seize the contents of inmate trust funds established for the inmate under Section 501.014.

nuggets.text: A county jail defendant who cannot pay a fine and costs can work them off (jail industries, workhouse, county farm or public projects), with each day of confinement and each day of labor rated at $150 toward the fine and costs.
nuggets.quote: rating such confinement at $150 for each day and rating such labor at $150 for each day

nuggets.text: A released person who is not required to report to a parole officer, or who may report outside Texas, gets $100 and TDCJ-paid transportation to a Texas residence or to a transit point TDCJ chooses.
nuggets.quote: If an inmate is released and is not required by the parole division to report to a parole officer or is authorized by the parole division to report to a location outside this state, the department shall provide the inmate with $100 and, at the expense of the department, transportation to: (1) the location of the inmate's residence, if the residence is in this state; or (2) a transit point determined appropriate by the department

nuggets.text: No release cash is given to a person who on discharge or release is transferred to a state jail felony facility, or who has a felony detainer and is released to another jurisdiction's custody.
nuggets.quote: Subsection (a)(3) does not apply to an inmate who on discharge or release on parole, mandatory supervision, or conditional pardon is transferred from the custody of the institutional division to a state jail felony facility or who is subject to a felony detainer and is released to the custody of another jurisdiction.

nuggets.text: On release TDCJ gives the person a copy of the permanent record of the work they did, their performance and their attendance in department work programs.
nuggets.quote: On release from imprisonment or supervision, the department shall provide the inmate, defendant, or releasee with a copy of a record made by the department under this section.

office.value: Texas Board of Criminal Justice sets any incentive pay scale and the private-industry wage deductions by rule; the Texas Department of Criminal Justice administers them

ordered_list.item: Reimbursement of the Health and Human Services Commission for assistance for the inmate's child's health needs
Any other court order, judgment, or writ
Then any unpaid balance owed to TDCJ under Government Code 501.063 (not in the downloaded statutes)

amount.value: not more than 80 percent of incentive pay may be deducted for restitution and dependent care
$100 at release on parole, mandatory supervision or conditional pardon ($50 on release, $50 on first report to a parole officer)
$100 and transportation home or to a transit point for a released person not required to report to a parole officer or allowed to report outside Texas
inmate lawsuit fees: the lesser of 20 percent of the preceding six months' deposits or the total, then the lesser of 10 percent of each month's deposits or the unpaid balance
county jail confinement and labor each rated at $150 a day toward unpaid fines and costs

answer: Texas minimum wage law excludes work while imprisoned in TDCJ's institutional division or confined in a local jail [N1]. The Board of Criminal Justice may (not must) set incentive pay [N2], paid into your trust fund, up to 80 percent deductible for restitution and dependent care [N3]. Correctional Industries pay is optional too [N4]. Private-industry (PIE) jobs pay at least the PIECP wage [N5]: the employer's wage for similar local work, or Workforce Commission data [N16], minus Board-set deductions [N6]. TDCJ pays court orders, including child support orders from anyone [N7], in order: child support, restitution, state child-health reimbursement [N8], court fees and costs, fines, other orders or writs [N9], before a Gov't Code 501.063 debt to TDCJ (not downloaded) [N11]. Your lawsuit fees take 20 percent of six months' deposits, then 10 percent monthly [N19]. TDCJ may recover supply, copay and property-damage debts [N10]; escape forfeits the account [N18]. For off-work-hours county sentences, judges may direct pay to dependents, expenses, jail upkeep and court debts [N14]; jail labor earns $150 a day toward unpaid fines and costs [N22]. Restitution centers deduct upkeep, travel, support and restitution [N15]. On discharge or release you get clothing, account money, an ID if available [N12], work record [N25] and cash: $100 plus a ride to your parole office ($50 leaving, $50 at first report) [N13], or, if you need not report, $100 plus a ride home or to a transit point [N23]; none on transfer to state jail or a felony detainer [N24].

out_of_corpus.where: Texas Board of Criminal Justice rules and TDCJ policy (Texas Administrative Code, Title 37, Part 6; TDCJ Inmate Trust Fund policy and the Offender Orientation Handbook), adopted under Gov't Code 497.004, 497.099 and 501.014

out_of_corpus.what: The actual percentages and recipients of deductions from private sector prison industries (PIE) wages, such as room and board, family support, the crime victims assistance account and savings
out_of_corpus.where: Texas Board of Criminal Justice rules on private sector prison industries programs (37 Tex. Admin. Code, Part 6) adopted under Gov't Code 497.0581 and 497.057

out_of_corpus.what: PIE programs, and TCI contracts with private businesses under Gov't Code 497.006(b), must meet federal certification rules: prevailing-wage pay and deductions limited to taxes, reasonable room and board, family support and victim compensation, capped at 80 percent of gross wages
out_of_corpus.where: 18 U.S.C. 1761(c) and the Bureau of Justice Assistance Prison Industry Enhancement Certification Program guideline

out_of_corpus.what: The inmate's unpaid balance owed to TDCJ (the inmate health care services fee) that 501.014(g) ranks behind court-ordered withdrawals
out_of_corpus.where: Tex. Gov't Code § 501.063 (statutes.capitol.texas.gov); cited by Gov't Code 501.014(g) but absent from the open-us-law download, where a bare '501.063' resolves to the unrelated Local Government Code § 501.063 (organizational meeting)

out_of_corpus.what: How a county jail work release, jail industries or work program runs, including any pay, fees and how earnings are handled
out_of_corpus.where: Commissioners court orders and sheriff rules (Local Gov't Code 351.201; CCP 42.034, 43.10), Texas Commission on Jail Standards rules (37 Tex. Admin. Code, Part 9), and the sentencing court's order under CCP 42.033

out_of_corpus.what: Payroll tax withholding on wages paid by outside or PIE employers
out_of_corpus.where: Internal Revenue Code withholding rules (Texas has no state income tax)

local_option: County programs are local: the commissioners court decides whether to set up a county jail industries program and the sheriff decides who participates (Local Gov't Code 351.201; revenue goes to the county for confinement costs, 351.202); the trial judge decides on county jail work release for low-risk defendants (CCP 42.034) and on off-work-hours or weekend service with employer deductions (CCP 42.033); a court may order a misdemeanant to repay the county $25 a day for jail confinement, billed by the sheriff on discharge (CCP 42.038); county jail labor pays no statutory wage: it earns one day off the sentence per day of labor (CCP 43.10) and, for someone unable to pay a fine and costs, $150 a day of credit toward them (CCP 43.09(a)), and the court or the sheriff may grant two additional days of credit per day served in an approved work program (CCP 43.09(d)).
notes: Scope is state prisoners in TDCJ, with county jail and restitution-center rules noted. Texas statutes make prison pay optional: 497.099(b) and 497.004(a) say the Board 'may' adopt an incentive pay scale, and Labor Code 62.156 removes minimum wage coverage for people imprisoned in the institutional division or confined in a local jail (it does not name state jail felony facilities, community residential facilities or restitution centers). Statutory wage floors exist only for outside-employer work: private sector prison industries (PIE) jobs must pay at least the PIECP wage (497.058, computed under 497.058(b)); other TCI contracts with private businesses must comply with all PIECP requirements (497.006(b)), which under federal law include prevailing wages; and TCI service contracts need only the federal minimum wage, with 497.058 not applying to them (497.006(c)(1), (e)). Ordinary TDCJ jobs carry no statutory wage. The 80 percent cap in 497.099(b) covers incentive pay only, not TCI or PIE pay. PIE deductions collected are forwarded to the comptroller for general revenue (497.056(a)). TDCJ has no statutory state-prison work release with a wage-distribution order; 508.119(g)-(h) let the parole division charge a fee capped at actual cost and grant limited release to seek or keep a job, but only to releasees already on parole or mandatory supervision placed in a community residential facility, so it is not incarceration and is not a gold section. The court-ordered withdrawal schedule in 501.014(e) is the only statutory 'order of priority' for state prisoners, and 501.014(g) puts those withdrawals ahead of the department's own 501.063 balance (Gov't Code 501.063 is cited but is not in the downloaded corpus). The CCP 42.033(b) list and the CCP 42A.607 list are statutory lists without the phrase 'order of priority'; 42.033 covers only sentences served intermittently during off-work hours or weekends, not 42.034 work release or jail industries; 42A.607 applies to defendants confined in a restitution center as a condition of community supervision. Under CCP 43.09(a) a day with both confinement and labor earns both $150 credits. Other trust-account reductions: court fees in an inmate's civil lawsuit (CPRC 14.006), garnishment (CPRC 63.007), seizure for intentional property damage after a hearing, with judicial review (Gov't Code 500.002), and forfeiture of the whole account on escape or attempted escape (501.014(d)). Release: the ID certificate in 501.015(a)(4) is obtained under 501.0165, and TDCJ may charge the inmate its actual costs or the Transportation Code 521.421 fee (501.0165(d)); 501.0155 adds the job training record (497.094) and work record for able-to-work inmates with a Texas residence, and 501.0166 has TDCJ request a birth certificate and Social Security card; these identity and employment documents are noted but not gold sections. A pre-parolee moving to parole receives any unpaid balance of the release money (499.002(c)). Arts and crafts sales (501.013) are not a prison job: proceeds first repay TDCJ-provided materials, with the rest to the inmate.
